findings.title: Make the movement guard concrete and correct the remaining work bounds
findings.body: The corrected plan still calls resize/reallocation movement exact without fixing a capacity-independent implementation. Array length alone cannot predict allocator copying or retained backing capacity. Specify a concrete changed-support strategy: for example fresh exact-length index/value arrays copied once per changed column, charging every copied/stored element plus old/new coexistence before replacement; or an explicitly conservative grow model with no assumed free resize. The cap must bound defined source-level element operations, not claim hidden allocator/native work is measured or zero. The claimed whole-update O(n^2) traversal bound still omits the O(w log n) binary lookups per panel, which sum to O(n^2 log n/b), and stable-ID incidence visits must scan all n IDs (O(n+h*w) for one outer pass), not merely the suffix w unless an additional ordering structure exists. Eligibility must finish before allocating a new workspace, so count its separate read traversal and gather. Require unchanged-support, support-change/copy, cap boundary, growth coexistence and adversarial support-change work-count fixtures. No gate or tolerance relaxation requested.

new_production_cost_verdict: No new production changes; R2 concerns proposed experiment work accounting.
